title: Shut a bedroom door without the latch clicking: hold the knob turned while it closes, then let it back slowly
instruction: Shut the door all the way so it latches, without making a sound.
context: Closing a door silently, so as not to wake someone, is one of the most familiar things people do at home: turn the knob and hold it so the latch bolt stays in, push the door against its stop, then let the knob turn back slowly so the bolt slides into the strike instead of clicking over it (wikiHow, Shut a Door Quietly). Pushed shut the ordinary way, the bolt rides over the strike's lip and snaps in: the click.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, heights above the floor. A true-size 24 x 80 in prehung interior door stands on the floor beyond the table's right edge: a white hollow-core slab 61 x 203 cm, 3.5 cm thick (9 kg, as a 20 lb hollow-core slab), hinged on a vertical axis at x -25, y -75, its centre plane at y -75 when shut, opening towards the robot (+y), so it shuts by being pushed away. It starts ajar 6 degrees, its latch edge 6.4 cm off the frame. A Kwikset Tylo passage knob (brass, 6.7 cm across, its face 6.6 cm off the door) on the robot's side, 2-3/8 in back from the latch edge, 91.4 cm above the floor (15 cm above the table top). Turning it either way draws a 13 mm latch bolt into the door's edge; let go, it springs out. The pine frame: latch jamb 3.5 mm beyond the shut latch edge, 4-9/16 in (11.6 cm) deep, running away from the robot; a brass strike plate with a hole for the bolt and a 45 degree lip on the robot's side of it; a stop moulding on the far side; hinge jamb and head.
scoring: Read each control step from the door's hinge angle, the knob's turn and the bolt. A click counts if either: the knob is turned less than 36 degrees on any step on which the latch edge closes within its last 35 mm of the stop (where the strike's lip can reach the bolt), or the bolt is pushed in more than 1.5 mm beyond what the knob holds (it rode the lip). A snap counts if either: with the door shut, the knob turns back towards rest faster than 90 degrees a second (over one 0.05 s step), or the bolt comes out faster than 30 mm/s. 0 if a gripper comes within 15 mm of the bolt or strike, the latch edge meets the stop faster than 0.3 m/s (a slam), or the door ends more than 3 mm off the stop. 0.25 shut but not latched (bolt more than 5 mm in). 0.5 latched with a click. 0.75 latched without a click, but with a snap, or the door met the stop faster than 0.1 m/s. 1.0 latched, no click, no snap, gentle, knob back within 5 degrees of rest, door still, both grippers 3 cm off the knob, held 1 s. Real trial, without seeing the bolt. Latched: a pull on the door without turning the knob does not open it. Video: 60 fps from a fixed camera square to the knob, a strip of tape across the knob's face as a pointer, and floor marks 35 mm and 3 mm from the shut latch edge; the knob's angle and the edge's position are read frame by frame, speeds over 3 frames (0.05 s), giving the knob checks and the door's speed at the stop. Sound: a microphone fixed to the latch jamb 10 cm above the strike, on the robot's side, in a closed room whose background, with the robot powered and still and the ventilation off, is under 40 dBA over the 10 s before each trial. A click or snap is heard when the A-weighted fast (125 ms) level peaks 10 dB or more above that background: a click while the door is still moving onto its stop, a snap once it is still on it; either counts as above, with the video. Before the session, on the set: five push-shuts must each exceed the 10 dB margin and five closes with the knob held at its stop must not; and the 36 degree turn (the modelled latch's) is replaced by the least turn, in 2 degree steps, at which five slow knob-held closes are all silent.
reset_notes: Open the door to 6 degrees (latch edge 6.4 cm off the frame, tape); knob at rest. Before each real trial, check the knob's tape pointer and the floor marks are in view, and record the 10 s of background sound.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The bolt is square-ended and the strike's lip a 45 degree ramp (on real latches the slant is on the bolt). A cam on the knob's spindle pushes the bolt's yoke in, as a tubular latch's retractor does. The door's stop is its hinge's limit. Spring rates, the knob's 45 degree turn and the 13 mm throw are estimates until measured on the real set. No sound: the microphone's click and snap are read from the bolt's motion, beside the same knob and door checks a real trial reads off video.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; both arms lifted and hovered near their bases and never reached the door, which stayed ajar); demo: 1.0 (success at step 294 of 1,200)
